newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Kaman picked for Australian order.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Kaman picked for Australian order.

text.p: Australian Defence Minister Ian McLachlan said on Friday that Kaman Aerospace International, a unit of Kaman Corp, had been selected as the preferred tenderer to supply 11 Kaman Sea Sprite helicopters for Australia's new ANZAC frigates.
Kaman was competing against GKN-Westland for the Australian order.

"Kaman was assessed as offering the best all round proposal for meeting (the Department of) Defence's demanding requirements with its Sea Sprite/Penguin (missile) combination of sensor and weapon systems as well as support through the life of the helicopter," McLachlan said in a statement.
The other contender was GKN-Westland which was offering its Super Lynx model. The SH-2G is remanufactured -- heavily refurbished -- from second-hand SH-2F airframes.
Australia and New Zealand were expected to buy the same helicopter, but New Zealand chose the Lynx last year.
Most of the Australian work would be associated with weapons systems integration, designing a flight simulator and creating a software support centre, the minister said.
"The primary role of the helicopters will be to increase the combat effecitiveness of the ANZAC frigate by providing over-the-horizon surveillance and targeting ability," he said.
The SH-2Gs would be fitted with the Penguin anti-ship missile built by Kongsberg Gruppen ASA of Norway.
Australia is building eight ANZAC Class frigates and plans to build 11 patrol ships, which it is calling Offshore Patrol Combatants.
Australian official sources said that if the patrol ship project goes ahead the Navy would certainly need more SH-2Gs.
The SH-2G uses the General Electric T700-401 engine.
The Australian navy already uses Sikorsky Seahawk helicopters on larger frigates, but needed a smaller model for the ANZACs and patrol ships.
The Defence Department invariably announces a preferred tenderer with which it conducts detail negotiations before signing a contract for new equipment.
